spatial_claims.claim: ABCD and CEFG are equiangular parallelograms with angle BCD equal to angle ECG
BC is placed in a straight line with CG (B, C, G are collinear)
Angle BCD + angle DCG = two right angles (angles on a straight line BCG)
Angle BCD + angle DCE = angle DCG (angle decomposition - INVALID but conclusion is correct)
DC and CE are in a straight line (D, C, E are collinear)
Parallelogram DCGK constructed with DC and CG as adjacent sides, K at intersection of line through G parallel to DC and line through D parallel to CG
A, D, K are collinear: AD parallel to BC and DK parallel to CG, both through D and both parallel to line BCG, so they coincide
ABCD and DCGK are between the same parallels (line BCG and line ADK)
ABCD : DCGK = BC : CG by Prop 6.1
K, G, F are collinear: KG parallel to DC and GF parallel to CE, since DCE is a straight line both are parallel to it and pass through G
DCGK and CEFG are between the same parallels (line DCE and line KGF)
DCGK : CEFG = DC : CE by Prop 6.1

configuration_map: Configuration at vertex C: Four rays emanate from C. Ray CB points left along the x-axis (180 deg), ray CG points right (0 deg). Ray CD points into the upper half-plane at angle (180 - alpha) from the positive x-axis, where alpha = angle BCD = angle ECG. Ray CE points into the lower half-plane at angle (360 - alpha), which is exactly 180 degrees opposite to ray CD, confirming D, C, E are collinear. Parallelogram DCGK: K is above line BCG, positioned so DK is parallel to CG and KG is parallel to DC. Point A is on line ADK (parallel to BCG through D), above the line. Point F is below line BCG on line KGF (through G, parallel to DCE). All collinearity claims (BCG, DCE, ADK, KGF) and all parallelism claims are mutually consistent and simultaneously realizable. The two applications of Prop 6.1 (Steps 4 and 5) use correctly identified shared parallels.
pass_reason: The spatial configuration is fully self-consistent. All collinearity claims (B-C-G, D-C-E, A-D-K, K-G-F) and parallelism relationships are mutually compatible. The applications of Prop 6.1 in Steps 4 and 5 correctly identify shared parallels. Step 2 contains a flawed angle algebra derivation (the claim 'angle BCD + angle DCE = angle DCG' is invalid), but the spatial conclusion it reaches (DC and CE form a straight line) is geometrically correct. All subsequent spatial reasoning depends only on this correct conclusion, not on the flawed intermediate step. The ratio compounding in Steps 6-7 is purely algebraic with no spatial content.
